newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Metsa Serla buys Swiss units.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Metsa Serla buys Swiss units.

text.p: Metsa-Serla Oy, Finland's third biggest forestry company, on Tuesday added to a brace of recent deals with a strategic agreement to buy part of troubled Swiss paper maker Biber Holding AG.

The company agreed to buy Biber's fine paper business Biberist, with annual net sales of around 1.5 billion markka ($325 million), for less than 300 million markka, which analysts found cheap -- but some voiced concern at Metsa-Serla's acquisitiveness.
The deal would add 330,000 tonnes/yr to Metsa-Serla's fine paper capacity to bring it over one million tonnes, making the company Europe's number three in coated fine paper, it said.
It follows a handful of trades in recent weeks as Metsa-Serla restructures to focus on printing and packaging.
Metsa-Serla, which last week agreed to buy mills from rival UPM-Kymmene Oy, also said it had sold a sawmill and completed the sale of its chemicals business to Swedish Kapital Industri.

"These (deals) including restructuring costs will slightly depress 1997 earnings...but they will have a significantly bigger positive impact on 1998 earnings," Metsa-Serla finance director Ari Martonen told a news conference.
The Swiss company has been loss-making -- its parent faces bankruptcy -- and Metsa-Serla said rationalisation talks would start at once.
"The deal will strengthen Metsa-Serla's position in its core businesses in central Europe," said Paivi Palomaki, analyst at Aktia Bank. "The price was not high when you compare it with sales.
"It was not a bad piece of news although Metsa-Serla has recently been acquiring quite heavily, which is a little bit worrying," she added.
At 1345 GMT, Metsa-Serla B traded 0.70 markka lower at 32.00, underperforming both the forest industry sub-index and the Helsinki bourse HEX all-share index.
Merita Bank analyst Pertti Aaltonen also expressed concern over Metsa-Serla's rash of acquisitions. "There are many balls in the air at the same time," he said.
Metsa-Serla's main owner, cooperative Metsaliitto, said it would now concentrate on incorporating the purchases.
"We've got quite a lot of work with these," Metsaliitto CEO Antti Oksanen told the news conference when asked if the company planned any further purchases.
He did not explicitly rule out any more deals -- Martonen said significant restructuring was expected in fine paper with about one-third of some 15 European companies on sale.

Metsa-Serla had a 254 million markka profit after financial items in January-August, down from 1.29 billion markka in 1995. Its full-year 1995 profit was 1.91 billion markka. ($ = 4.619 Finnish Markka)
